summary:
The Heidelberg Catechism, which the Reformed Church in America holds as one of its standards, teaches that a person is righteous before God only by true faith in Jesus Christ: God, without any merit of the person but of mere grace, grants and counts to them the perfect satisfaction, righteousness and holiness of Christ, as though they had never sinned and had fully obeyed. The catechism explains that faith is not the ground of acceptance, since only Christ's satisfaction is, and that faith is the only way the person can receive it. The questions read do not address election in the sense of God's eternal choice or whether believers can fall away.

The Canons of Dort, which the Reformed Church in America holds as one of its standards, teach that election is God's unchangeable purpose, made before the foundation of the world out of mere grace, by which he chose from the fallen human race a certain number of persons to redemption in Christ, though they were no better or more deserving than others, and decreed to give them faith, justification and sanctification. Not all are elected: others are passed by in the eternal decree and left in the misery they plunged themselves into, and are condemned for their unbelief and their other sins. The articles read do not address justification or perseverance in the terms of this topic.

points.question: How are you righteous before God?
points.answer: Only by true faith in Jesus Christ: God, without any merit of ours but of mere grace, grants and counts to us the perfect satisfaction, righteousness and holiness of Christ, as if we had never sinned, when we receive it with a believing heart.

points.question: Why say "by faith only"?
points.answer: Not because faith is worthy in itself, but because only Christ's satisfaction, righteousness and holiness is our righteousness before God, and faith is the only way we can receive and apply it.

points.question: Did God choose who would be saved?
points.answer: Yes. Election is the unchangeable purpose of God, before the foundation of the world and out of mere grace, to choose from the fallen human race a certain number of persons to redemption in Christ, giving them faith, justification and sanctification, though they are by nature neither better nor more deserving.
points.at: Canons of Dort, First Head, Article 7

points.question: What of those not chosen?
points.answer: Not all but some only are elected, while others are passed by in the eternal decree: God decreed to leave them in the common misery they wilfully plunged themselves into and not to give them saving faith, and to condemn them at last for the declaration of his justice, on account of their unbelief and their other sins.
points.at: Canons of Dort, First Head, Article 15

election.at: Canons of Dort, First Head, Articles 7, 15

review.note: The Heidelberg Catechism: Questions 60 and 61 read in full on 2026-11-12 in the CCEL text; Q. 59 and 62-64, which say more about good works, were not read in full. The RCA's own copy was not compared. Election and perseverance are left "not stated" for the Heidelberg Catechism because they are not addressed in the questions read; the Canons of Dort cover election. Not yet checked by a second reviewer. The Canons of Dort: Articles 7 and 15 of the First Head read on 2026-11-12 in the URCNA English text. The rest of the Canons, including the Fifth Head on the perseverance of the saints, which would answer the third question, was not read, so perseverance is left "not stated". The RCA's own copy and its adoption of the Canons are unchecked. Not yet checked by a second reviewer.
